title: A coequalizer presentation with finite supports is a filtered colimit of finite coequalizers
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space; sheaves of sets on $X$ are those on the site of open subsets of $X$ with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and coproducts, coequalizers and colimits below are taken in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $A,B$ be sets, $U_a,V_b\subseteq X$ open and $S_a,T_b$ sets ($a\in A$, $b\in B$), with $j_{U!}\underline S$ the extension by the empty set [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty]. For $A'\subseteq A$ let $(C_{A'},(\iota^{A'}_a)_{a\in A'})$ be a coproduct of $(j_{U_a!}\underline{S_a})_{a\in A'}$ and for $A'\subseteq A''$ let $\kappa_{A''A'}:C_{A'}\to C_{A''}$ be the morphism with $\kappa_{A''A'}\iota^{A'}_a=\iota^{A''}_a$; write $C=C_A$, $\kappa_{A'}=\kappa_{AA'}$; define $D_{B'}$, $\delta_{B''B'}$, $D=D_B$, $\delta_{B'}=\delta_{BB'}$ in the same way for $(j_{V_b!}\underline{T_b})_{b\in B}$. Let $r,s:D\rightrightarrows C$ be morphisms and $q:C\to\mathcal F$ a coequalizer of $r,s$. Assume (finite supports, as in [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-finite-relation-truncations]): for every finite $B'\subseteq B$ there is a finite $A'\subseteq A$ such that $r\delta_{B'}$ and $s\delta_{B'}$ both factor through $\kappa_{A'}$. Let $\Lambda$ be the set of pairs $\lambda=(B',A')$ of finite subsets $B'\subseteq B$, $A'\subseteq A$ such that $r\delta_{B'}=\kappa_{A'}r_\lambda$ and $s\delta_{B'}=\kappa_{A'}s_\lambda$ for some morphisms $r_\lambda,s_\lambda:D_{B'}\to C_{A'}$, ordered by $(B',A')\le(B'',A'')$ iff $B'\subseteq B''$ and $A'\subseteq A''$. Then: (1) $r_\lambda,s_\lambda$ are uniquely determined by $\lambda$, and $\Lambda$ is a directed set (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound); (2) for $\lambda=(B',A')$ let $q_\lambda:C_{A'}\to\mathcal F_\lambda$ be a coequalizer of $r_\lambda,s_\lambda$; for $\lambda\le\mu=(B'',A'')$ there is a unique morphism $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}:\mathcal F_\lambda\to\mathcal F_\mu$ with $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}q_\lambda=q_\mu\kappa_{A''A'}$, and a unique $c_\lambda:\mathcal F_\lambda\to\mathcal F$ with $c_\lambda q_\lambda=q\kappa_{A'}$; these satisfy $\varphi_{\lambda\lambda}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{\nu\mu}\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=\varphi_{\nu\lambda}$ and $c_\mu\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=c_\lambda$; (3) $(\mathcal F,(c_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda})$ is a colimit of the system $(\mathcal F_\lambda,\varphi_{\mu\lambda})$ over $\Lambda$ in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$. Thus $\mathcal F$ is a directed colimit of coequalizers of pairs of maps between finite coproducts of sheaves $j_{U!}\underline S$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (the truncated relations and the directed set).* By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-coproduct-finite-subcoproducts](2) every $\kappa_{A''A'}$ ($A'\subseteq A''\subseteq A$) is injective on sections over every open $W$, hence a monomorphism of sheaves: if $\kappa_{A''A'}f=\kappa_{A''A'}g$ for $f,g:\mathcal G\to C_{A'}$, then $f_W=g_W$ for every $W$. Since $\kappa_{A'}$ is a monomorphism, $r_\lambda,s_\lambda$ are unique for $\lambda=(B',A')\in\Lambda$. For $\lambda\le\mu=(B'',A'')$ the two morphisms $\kappa_{A''A'}r_\lambda$ and $r_\mu\delta_{B''B'}$ agree after composing with the monomorphism $\kappa_{A''}$: $\kappa_{A''}\kappa_{A''A'}r_\lambda=\kappa_{A'}r_\lambda=r\delta_{B'}=r\delta_{B''}\delta_{B''B'}=\kappa_{A''}r_\mu\delta_{B''B'}$ (the identities $\kappa_{A''}\kappa_{A''A'}=\kappa_{A'}$, $\delta_{B''}\delta_{B''B'}=\delta_{B'}$ hold on each summand by the uniqueness in the universal property of the coproduct [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]); hence $\kappa_{A''A'}r_\lambda=r_\mu\delta_{B''B'}$, and likewise $\kappa_{A''A'}s_\lambda=s_\mu\delta_{B''B'}$. $\Lambda$ is nonempty: $D_\emptyset$ and $C_\emptyset$ are initial objects, so $(\emptyset,\emptyset)\in\Lambda$ with $r_{(\emptyset,\emptyset)}=s_{(\emptyset,\emptyset)}$ the unique map. Upper bounds: for $(B_1,A_1),(B_2,A_2)\in\Lambda$ put $B_3=B_1\cup B_2$, $A_3=A_1\cup A_2$ and let $r_3:D_{B_3}\to C_{A_3}$ be the morphism with $r_3\iota^{B_3}_b=\kappa_{A_3A_i}r_{(B_i,A_i)}\iota^{B_i}_b$ for any $i$ with $b\in B_i$ (if $b\in B_1\cap B_2$ the two choices agree, since both become $r\iota^B_b$ after composing with the monomorphism $\kappa_{A_3}$); then $\kappa_{A_3}r_3\iota^{B_3}_b=\kappa_{A_i}r_{(B_i,A_i)}\iota^{B_i}_b=r\delta_{B_i}\iota^{B_i}_b=r\delta_{B_3}\iota^{B_3}_b$ for every $b$, so $\kappa_{A_3}r_3=r\delta_{B_3}$, and the same for $s$; so $(B_3,A_3)\in\Lambda$ is an upper bound.

proof.text: *Step 3 (every index occurs).* For $a\in A$, $\lambda_a:=(\emptyset,\{a\})\in\Lambda$ ($D_\emptyset$ is initial). For $b\in B$, the finite-support hypothesis applied to $B'=\{b\}$ gives a finite $A_b\subseteq A$ with $(\{b\},A_b)=:\lambda_b\in\Lambda$. (Here $C_{\{a\}}=j_{U_a!}\underline{S_a}$ with $\iota^{\{a\}}_a=\mathrm{id}$, and $\kappa_{\{a\}}=\iota^A_a$.)

proof.text: *Step 4 (existence of the induced map).* Let $(M,(\mu_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda})$ be a cocone on the system, $\mu_\nu\varphi_{\nu\lambda}=\mu_\lambda$. Let $v:C\to M$ be the morphism with $v\iota^A_a=\mu_{\lambda_a}q_{\lambda_a}$ for all $a$ (universal property of the coproduct [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]). For every $\lambda=(B',A')$ we have $v\kappa_{A'}=\mu_\lambda q_\lambda$: on the summand $a\in A'$, $\lambda_a\le\lambda$ and $\mu_\lambda q_\lambda\iota^{A'}_a=\mu_\lambda q_\lambda\kappa_{A'\{a\}}=\mu_\lambda\varphi_{\lambda\lambda_a}q_{\lambda_a}=\mu_{\lambda_a}q_{\lambda_a}=v\iota^A_a=v\kappa_{A'}\iota^{A'}_a$. Then $vr=vs$: on the summand $b\in B$ (Step 3), $vr\iota^B_b=vr\delta_{\{b\}}=v\kappa_{A_b}r_{\lambda_b}=\mu_{\lambda_b}q_{\lambda_b}r_{\lambda_b}=\mu_{\lambda_b}q_{\lambda_b}s_{\lambda_b}=vs\iota^B_b$. So there is exactly one $u:\mathcal F\to M$ with $uq=v$ (coequalizer [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]), and $uc_\lambda=\mu_\lambda$ for every $\lambda$, because $uc_\lambda q_\lambda=uq\kappa_{A'}=v\kappa_{A'}=\mu_\lambda q_\lambda$ and $q_\lambda$ is an epimorphism (Step 2).

source.place: Modules, proof of Lemma Tag 0CAI (lemma-filtered-colimit-constructibles), lines 3058-3064: 'Thus our sheaf is the colimit of the cokernels of these maps between finite coproducts'

proof.text: *Step 5 (uniqueness; conclusion).* If $u':\mathcal F\to M$ satisfies $u'c_\lambda=\mu_\lambda$ for all $\lambda$, then $u'q\iota^A_a=u'q\kappa_{\{a\}}=u'c_{\lambda_a}q_{\lambda_a}=\mu_{\lambda_a}q_{\lambda_a}=v\iota^A_a$ for every $a$, so $u'q=v=uq$ and $u'=u$ since $q$ is an epimorphism. Hence $(\mathcal F,(c_\lambda))$ is a colimit of the system over the directed set $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], which is (3). (Stacks states this as 'our sheaf is the colimit of the cokernels'; the verification above is the universal property written out. It is equivalent to interchanging the colimit over $\Lambda$ with the coequalizer, Categories Lemma Tag 002M, together with the cofinality of $\Lambda$ in the finite subsets of $A$ and of $B$ (Step 3) and [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-coproduct-finite-subcoproducts](1); the direct check avoids the cofinality argument. Stacks' phrase is not 'finite colimits commute with filtered colimits', which would not apply here.)
